name: JavaClaw

overview_markdown:
JavaClaw is a Java 25 / Spring Boot 4 reimplementation of the OpenClaw personal AI assistant, originally created as a demo for JobRunr and now positioned as a community-driven Java agent platform. It acts as a local control plane: a Spring Modulith core (`base/` and `app/`) handles the agent loop, task management, and configuration, while channel plugins (Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp via wacli, WebSocket chat) and tool plugins (Brave search, Playwright browser automation) self-register via Spring Boot auto-configuration. LLM access goes through Spring AI with pluggable providers — OpenAI, Anthropic (including Claude Code OAuth), Google GenAI, and local Ollama — selectable during a guided onboarding flow.

Its standout differentiator is durable background job processing via JobRunr (with a dashboard on :8081), letting the agent schedule one-off, delayed, and cron-recurring tasks stored as human-readable Markdown files. Recent commits show active hardening: ArchUnit-enforced module boundaries, token-by-token WebSocket streaming, multi-model provider support with an agents management page, and careful security fixes like refusing WhatsApp group chats to prevent group members from instructing a shell-capable agent.

Compared to OpenClaw, JavaClaw trades ecosystem breadth and runtime lightness for JVM familiarity and enterprise-grade structure. It keeps data local (embedded H2, file-backed workspace) with no telemetry, but the agent has unrestricted shell and file access with no sandboxing layer, so it carries the same high shell-risk profile as other local agents. There are no official releases yet, so expect a moving target.
